questions.answer: As social media is used more and more extensively, there is a growing awareness of the importance of using it properly and responsibly. While it broadens perspectives and connects people, its potential drawbacks, such as spreading misinformation and causing cognitive overload, remind us to maintain a critical mindset. To maximize the positive function of social media, it is crucial to develop the ability to screen information effectively. Users should actively filter out low-quality content and stay focused on valuable information such as industry insight and professional knowledge. By doing so, users not only prevent themselves from wasting time on mindless scrolling but also convert social platforms into powerful self-improvement tools that foster sustained growth in cognitive and professional competence. More importantly, social media users act as both information consumers and online environment contributors, and each of their online actions can have far-reaching social impacts. Therefore, it is necessary for users to comply with codes of conduct such as refraining from spreading fake news, resisting cyberbullying, respecting personal privacy, and ensure accountability for their words and actions online. In conclusion, the proper and responsible use of social media extends beyond individual benefit to collective obligation. By cultivating critical thinking and adhering to ethical standards, we can together foster a safer, healthier and more inclusive online environment for all.

blocks.transcriptDraft: Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owner's commands and gestures. But are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training? To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures. The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location, despite having never received prior training. The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans. This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans. Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago. This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet. Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits so that they could function as companions and workers. This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures. However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability. Why does this matter? Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world. They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained and are behaviorally wild. Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem. Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior may help alleviate this problem. According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures. They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision. Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect and giving them space the researchers assert can reduce much conflict.

你是否认为你的冰箱就是一个充满均匀冷气的大箱子 ？ 并非如此 ！ 普通冰箱内部的温度实际上从前往
后 、 从下到上乃至中间各处都不尽相同 。 正因如此 ， 冰箱内食品的摆放位置远比你可能意识到的要重要得多 。
现代冰箱的全部作用在于减缓细菌生长 ， 细菌在 4 · 4 一 60 ℃ 的温度下会迅速繁殖 。 因此 ， 冰箱温度通常会
设定在或低于这个低温末端 （ 4 · 4 ℃ ） ， 以防止食物受到细菌侵害 。
尽管花时间整理冰箱看似会破坏你一天的心情 ， 但实际上这样做会让冰箱更方便使用 、 更容易清洁 ， 也更
符合食品安全要求 。
冰箱门内侧的那些小储物格虽然很方便 ， 但它们无法维持恒定的温度 ， 因此切勿将易腐烂变质的食物存
放在那里 。
冰箱顶部区域的温度高于冰箱底部 ， 所以留此区域存放不需要特别低温保存的食物 。 即食食品或熟食可
存放在上层搁架上 。
中层搁架是冰箱内温度控制最稳定的区域 ， 因此可将鸡蛋存放于此 。 如果上层搁架空间不够 ， 饮料和即
食食品也可以存放在中层搁架上 。
底层搁架的里头是冰箱内温度最低的地方 ， 可将易变质的乳制品存放此处 ， 以延长其食用期限 。 切勿将
含水量高的食物存放此处 ， 因为其中的水分会结冰 ， 实际上会糟蹋掉这类食物 。
blocks.transcriptDraft: Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air? Not so. The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top, and everywhere in between. Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realise. The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius. As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria. Although it might seem like time spent organising the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user friendly, easier to clean, and food safety conscious. Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there. The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra chilly temperatures. Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf. The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here. Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you were in out of room up top. The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer. Never store foods with high water content here because the water within them can and will freeze effectively ruining them.

blocks.title: Recording One
blocks.translation:
我目前的研究主要聚焦于压力等因素及其对我们免疫系统的影响 。 因此 ， 我现在尤为感兴趣的项目都聚
焦于老年人这一人群以及对他们有重大影响的因素 。 在其中一个项目中 ， 我们正在研究老年人髖骨骨折
这是一种常见情况一一一并且我们也正试图了解抑郁症对这种情况产生的影响 。 因髋骨骨折住院的患者往往
会患上抑郁症 ， 而这类人群往往比其他人更快走向衰弱 。 他们会感染疾病 ， 而且这些感染通常会导致他们死
亡 。 因此 ， 我们正尝试减缓这种走向衰弱的进程 。 所以 ， 如果我们能更好地了解这些因素如何相互作用 ， 那么
我们就能真正开始采取一些应对措施了 。
我的研究将带来的重大影响在伯明翰最先惠及的显然是老年人 ， 因为他们正是髋骨骨折并患上抑郁症的
群体 ， 我们正努力改善他们的健康状况和生活质量 。 但这不仅仅是伯明翰乃至整个英国的问题 ， 这是一个全
球性问题 。 人口正在老龄化 ： 老年一代的人口越来越多 ， 寿命更长 ， 但他们在人生中的大部分时间里未必能保
持健康 ； 因此 ， 他们晚年常常疾病缠身 ， 而我们正试图了解那些有助于提升晚年生活质量的因素 。
我认为我的研究最让我兴奋的地方在于它切实且具有现实意义 。 许多学者可能对自己的研究充满热情 ，
但他们的研究或许与周围的人关联不大 。 然而 ， 我觉得我所做的工作与每个人都息息相关 ， 因为每个人都在
变老 ； 健康是所有人的议题 ， 无关年龄 ， 而我正在努力做的是了解影响健康的因素并探究我们怎样才能改善人
们的生活质量 。 这就是它真正让我兴奋的原因之一
另一点在于 ， 我们不再局限于单一视角一一也就是说 ， 不再仅从心理学家的角度来研究衰老与健康 ， 而是
把许许多多不同的技术与观点整合起来 ， 切实研究影响健康的各类因素 。
blocks.transcriptDraft: My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system. So the current projects that I'm quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them. In one project, we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event, and we're trying to understand the impact of depression. Often people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that but then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others. They get infections, often these infections lead to death. So we're trying to slow down that progression to feebleness. So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it. The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people, Because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression, and we're trying to improve their health and their quality of life. But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK. This is a problem globally. People are aging, there's a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer, but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives. So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health, and we're trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on. I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant. Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them. Because I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone, because everyone is aging. Health is an issue for everyone regardless of their age, and what I'm trying to do is understand the factors that affect health and how we can improve the quality of life in people. So that's one of the things that really excites me about it. One of the other things is rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health, just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.

元 。 之所以有这样庞大的市场 ， 部分原因在于 ， 大多数大学和研究生院并不教授基础的组织方法 。 但是烹饪

让厨房高效运作的体系被称为 ” 五 5 “ ” 一 “ e ， 字面意思是 “ 放置就位 ” 。 它是一个法语短语 ， 意思是收集

天中的每一环节了然于心

们为一次三小时的晚宴轮班很可能就要做六小时的准备工作 。 “ 放置就位 ” 迫使厨师将自己的每一分钟时间
和每一个规范动作都纳入责任管理之中 。 “ 一道菜所需的所有食材都要放在一个特定的位置 ， 这样他们的手
实际上就只需要移动几英寸 ， ” 美国烹饪学院讲师德韦恩 · 利图马解释道 ， “ 一旦学生布置好自己的工作台 ， 即使我
遮住他们的眼睛 ， 他们也应该能够知道自己的刀一直放在这里 ， 油一直放在这里 ， 而盐和胡椒也一直放在这里 。 ”
而若将 “ 放置就位 ” 发挥至极致 ， 它就会告诉我们 ： 时间是宝贵的 。 资源是宝贵的 。 空间是宝贵的 。 你的
自尊和他人的尊重也同样是宝贵的 。 要明智地使用它们 。 这难道不是一种我们这个时代的处世哲学吗 ？
blocks.transcriptDraft: Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs. We talk about them and try to eat like them. But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques? According to market data enterprises, Americans spend nearly $10 billion a year on self-help and personal organisation products. The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organisation, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do. Perhaps the principles of cooking organisation can be extended to help even those of us who aren't top chefs. The system that makes kitchens function is called means on-plus, or literally put in place. It's a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking. But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper. Some cooks call it their religion. It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labour and material and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline. Students at the Culinary Institute of America view it as a way of life. It's a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment to kind of rid themselves of distractions. And it's a habit that some students carry with them even when they're not in the kitchen. They mise en place their life. They set up their books for class. They set up their chef whites. they shine their shoes, they know everything that they need every step of the day. Then how does one attain this level of organisation? The key to high level organisation is the mindset. Coox can easily do six hours of preparation for a three-hour dinner shift. Mies en place forces Coox to account for every minute of their time and every movement. Every component of one single dish is in one single corner, so their hand literally moves inches, explains Dwayne Limpuma, an instructor at the Culinary Institute of America. Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes and they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here. But practised at its highest level, mise en place says that time is precious. Resources are precious. Space is precious. Your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely. Isn't that a philosophy for our time?

blocks.title: Recording Three
blocks.translation:
为什么我们不再为自己设定目标 ， 在生活中不再追求进步 ？ 其中一个原因是 ， 我们认为应该接纳真实的
自己 ， 而非一味地追求自我提升 。 我们在此问题上所犯的错误在于 ， 尽管自我接纳非常重要 ， 但它实际上应该
被用作我们成长的基础 。 当我们不再成长 、 学习 、 追求生活的改善 ， 我们往往会停滞不前 ， 接受现状 ， 不再相信
自己可以变得更好
创设目标并取得进步的一个重要工具就是发挥我们的想象力 。 然而 ， 通常情况下 ， 当我们步入中年之时 ，
我们已经不再憧憬想要达成什么样的目标 ， 对设定目标也缺乏热情 。 我们没有因为实现目标而感到自信 、 快
乐和满足 ， 反而觉得自己总是达不到目标 。 这会导致失望 ， 我们就会不再梦想未来 。 我们不再去想象我们想
要的理想生活或想成为的人 ， 很快就会被现实的痛苦击垮 。
到目前为止 ， 除非我们从事创意行业 ， 否则我们会觉得 “ 玩耍 " 这一概念有些幼稚 。 在西方社会 ， 我们大多
是用头脑一一也就是理性思维来行事 。 但人们开始逐渐理解这个概念 ， 因为运用想象力其实是我们能做的最
强大的事情之一
我们因未能达成目标而感到恼怒的问题在于 ： 目标总是在变化 ， 而我们也总是在不断适应 ， 无论我们是否
意识到了这一点 。 因此 ， 最终的结果就是我们会觉得自己永远无法实现目标 。 而这正是最大的误解之一 ， 也
是导致失败 、 不满和不幸的原因 。 我们总是以目标作为评判标准 ， 而不是以过程 （ 即我们所走过的路 ） 作为衡
量标准 。 丹 · 沙利文把这个现象称为 “ 差距与成果 ” 。 我们总是以那个永远无法实现的目标来评判自己 ， 而不
是去衡量我们在过程中所取得的成果 。 如果以过程而非以我们想要达成的目标为衡量标准 ， 我们就能看到成
果 。 我们也会看到那些被我们视为理所当然或忽视的东西 。 这是一个简单但深刻的认知转变 ， 我喜欢它的地
方在于 ， 它有立即让人提升一个层次的力量 。 它真的非常简单 ， 却能立即对我们的思维产生积极的影响 。
Part Reading Comprehension
blocks.transcriptDraft: Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life? One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves. The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth. When we are not growing, learning, and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what is, and stop believing we can be better. A key tool for creating goals and progressing is using our imagination. Yet, as is so often the case, by the time we've reached mid-life, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve, and feel quite negatively about goal-setting. Instead of feeling confidence, happiness, and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short. That leads to disappointment and we stop dreaming. We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be. Quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality. Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we've found the idea of using play a bit childish. In the West, we're mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind. But it's beginning to be better understood because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do. The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting whether we realize it or not. What happens therefore is that we end up feeling like we are never going to reach our goals. And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness. We measure against the goal rather than where we've come from. Dan Sullivan calls this the gap and the gain. We measure always against the goal which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain that is where we've come from. In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. We see things we've taken for granted or not noticed. It's a simple yet profound change in perception. And what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear. It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate positive impact on our thinking.
